## 1. Executive summary

<One paragraph. Three sentences ideal, never more than five. Open with the
decision in front of the executive team, in plain language. Name the
recommendation if the brief makes one (commit / reshape / kill). Name the
single most-important kill-shot risk by short label. Close with the
revised commitment criteria section pointer.>

## 2. Kill-shot risks

Three to five risks. Each risk is a paragraph, not a bullet. Each risk has
the precondition under which it becomes the killing failure.

manifest.>

**Precondition:** <what has to be true for this risk to become the failure>

## 4. Revised commitment criteria

The pre-mortem's job is to update the conditions under which "commit" is
the right call.

### Conditions for COMMIT
- <Condition 1: specific, measurable, time-bound>
- <Condition 2>
- <Condition 3>

### Conditions for RESHAPE
- <What about the plan would have to change. Be specific: what to add,
  what to drop, what to delay.>

### Conditions for KILL
- <The threshold below which we walk away. Often the inverse of one or
  two of the COMMIT conditions.>

If a risk has no named owner, it is not actually being mitigated.
